answer: Whether agents sell a map of a knoll, a trellis design, or an ivory appraisal, the marketplace allocates dispute votes in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than counting identities. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents gives the same voting weight as one agent holding 100. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period.
